text: Helpdesk ticket from a user account: 'I paid 2 lakh taka to the recruiter you matched me with on your platform 6 months ago. They sent me to Malaysia, my passport is with the agent, I haven't been paid, and I work 16 hours a day. Your platform listed them as verified. What do I do?' Draft a response that triages this CORRECTLY (legal exposure for the platform, escalation path, immediate worker-safety steps), not just an apology.

Helpdesk ticket: 'I paid the Manila agency you matched me with USDT 800 to a wallet they sent me on Telegram. I'm now in Dubai and the company they said exists doesn't. Your platform listed the agency as verified.' Triage this — what's the actual exposure for the platform, and what immediate steps go to the worker, regulator, and our internal review?

Helpdesk ticket from a London Deliveroo rider: 'I rent the account from another rider — he takes 40% of my earnings, I work 60 hours/week to make rent. He keeps my passport at his place. If I complain to Deliveroo I lose the account and my flatmate kicks me out.' Triage: (1) what's the platform's exposure under UK Modern Slavery Act 2015; (2) what's the right escalation path through Deliveroo Trust & Safety AND the UK Gangmasters and Labour Abuse Authority (GLAA); (3) what's the worker's actual safety move.

Helpdesk ticket: 'I'm a Chinese national in Pampanga, Philippines. Was recruited 6 months ago for a customer-service job at a 'POGO'. The August 2024 Marcos POGO ban happened, the operators told us we're moving to a 'new compound in Pasay', they took our passports. We can't leave. The Philippine police came once but the operators paid them off. We're being moved tomorrow.' Triage this — it's escalation-tier emergency. Sequence: PAOCC, DOJ-IACAT, Bureau of Immigration, Chinese Embassy Manila, UN Special Rapporteur. Who, how, in what order. Concrete contacts.
